meaning: Praise, divine sparks, and spiritual restoration
description: In 1 Chronicles 25:7, 288 singers are mentioned who were trained to sing for the Lord, all masters in their craft. These Levitical singers formed the core of the Temple's musical service and represented praise as a central part of worship. In Kabbalistic tradition, the number 288 has acquired an expanded symbolic meaning connected to divine sparks that must be gathered to restore cosmic order. Thus, the number 288 carries a deep dual symbolism: praise in the sanctuary and spiritual restoration.

versions.meaning: The number 288 is linked to the 288 Levitical singers in the Temple and to Kabbalistic concepts of divine sparks.
versions.description: In 1 Chronicles 25:7, 288 singers are mentioned who were trained to sing for the Lord, all of them masters in their art. In kabbalistic tradition, especially in Lurianic Kabbalah, the number 288 refers to the 288 divine sparks (nitzotzot) that were scattered at creation's "breaking of the vessels" (shevirat ha-kelim), and which must be gathered to restore cosmic order (tikkun). These two traditions give the number 288 a deep symbolic meaning connected with praise, sanctuary, and spiritual restoration.

footnotes.text: In Lurianic Kabbalah, 288 refers to the 288 divine sparks (nitzotzot) that were scattered during the "breaking of the vessels" (shevirat ha-kelim). According to this tradition, these sparks must be gathered through holy acts to restore cosmic order (tikkun olam).
The 288 singers were divided into 24 groups of 12 each, corresponding to the 24 priestly divisions that served in the Temple (1 Chron. 25:1–31).
